utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar -- one moment. Let the accused sit down. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam and good morning to you too. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and also good morning to my colleagues of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with co-counsel, Ms. Joanne Richardson, Ms. Patricia Sellers, and our acting case manager is Ms. Sanja Bokulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you too, Mr. Wubben and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, my learned friends. My name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic. Also Jasmina Cosic and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Before we proceed with the cross-examination, any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Last Friday, Your Honours, we filed the response to the 92 bis motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't received it as yet. What we received is a Prosecution response to Defence motion to add a number of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's included. That's what I meant, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean it's included? That's what you meant, I see. And Prosecution response to Defence motion to admit the evidence of a witness in the form of a written statement pursuant to the Rule 92 bis. That's what we got as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We are still waiting for your Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's due today, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I misunderstood you. In the meantime on Friday also the Defence filed confidentially a further communication regarding non-compliance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour and we aim to file a response to that on coming Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So shall we bring the witness, in?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the meantime we please apologise, I have to address urgent matters and I was to be available for these preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have to go elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Wubben, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can let me know if you will both be available after Wednesday, between Wednesday and Friday to have a sit down with our Senior Legal Officer and try to work out a schedule to finish your testimony more or less we will try and work it out, all right? I'll ask Mr. Wubben -- not Mr. Wubben, Mr. Von Hebel to contact you and he will try to work that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good Morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope you've had a good rest and are ready to continue and finish this cross-examination. If there are at any time problems with interpretation, please draw our attention straight away. Yes, Ms. Sellers. Cross-examined by Ms. Sellers: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Are you able to hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Friday we were turning our attention to the attack on August 8th of Jezestica and I believe one of the last questions I was asking you concerned the feelings in the community within the geographical area from which you come, concerning crimes committed during World War II. My specific question is that you've testified about crimes committed by the Eric family. Do you agree with me that there was animosity in that area concerning war crimes that dated from World War II?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware that the animosity was on both sides, both with Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Far less among the Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you have knowledge that the town or the village of Jezestica was attacked during World War II and resulted in deaths and damage to property?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about World War II, if you mean attacked by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, what would -- yes, what would become what we call today the Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of your knowledge of 1992, then, you said were you aware that Jezestica was attacked. Are you also aware that during that attack, that parts of the upper village were burned, was burned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know that it was burnt but I did know that before that, Serbs from Jezestica attacked the Muslims of Ejub Golic's group and that on the 8th of August 1992, Nurif Rizvanovic and his fighters helped Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that during that attack, of both Nurif Rizvanovic and Ejub Golic in Jezestica that there were deaths and it was reported that one person's head was cut off after death? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know about that. All I knew was that two of Nurif Rizvanovic's fighters went missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could I clarify one thing with you? Do you know what time the attack on Jezestica started on August 8th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Jezestica, you can't know exactly when the attack began. The Serbs were attacking and then both sides continued attacking so it went on all day from the morning, starting from the morning, and then throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that when Nurif Rizvanovic came, that some of the soldiers from his unit then placed themselves in other groups of fighting men. Do you remember that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do. On the 8th of August, about ten men from Nurif's group remained, those who were attacking Jezestica, they remained with Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Nurif Rizvanovic had about 400 or upwards, let's say 350 men in his group, soldiers in his group, and do you know whether any other -- other than the ten that you've mentioned -- if any other soldiers went to different groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One couldn't know for sure, precisely. Some even went back to Tuzla. Whether they went elsewhere, I really didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the participation of other Bosnian Muslim fighters or soldiers in the attack or on the attack on the 8th of August in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only those two groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Andrici was also part of the attack on the 8th of August as was Zaluzje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Andrici is very part from this part of Jezestica. It was impossible to know that. It's about 25 kilometres away, which is really far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know that Zaluzje was part of the attacks that occurred on the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also far from where I was. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could have some very short video clips be shown at this time using Sanctions. Your Honour, the clips come from Prosecution Exhibit 328 and 329.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you to look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "And then I remembered something else again, when we did this -- whether we did this on the same day as that, the units that were around Bljeceva and Cizmici and Pale and Glogova, that is the unit from Glogova, at that time there were already quite a lot of people from Glogova who were armed. They had the task that with the help of people from Konjevic Polje, Nurif Rizvanovic, and together with -- I'm sorry, with the help of Nurif Rizvanovic, that is Nurif, N-u-r-i-f, Rizvanovic, R-i-z-a-n-o-v-i-c, who had come from Tuzla with 400 armed fighters. They had the task of entering Glogova. In other words, that they -- they go through Siljkovici, is it Siljkovici? And -- okay. And Jezestica. Okay. So by attacking through the hill, mountain of Siljkovici, that's S-i-l-j-k-o-v-i-c-i, and the hamlet of Jezestica, that's J-e-z-e-s-t-i-c-a, that they would then enter Glogova. So they were supposed to carry out a breakthrough so that on the same day that we went into Zalazje, that they would go into Glogova."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have just one technical question. That was very dark on one of the screens and it was lighter on another one of our screens. I just want to know, sir, were you able to see the people in the video clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With difficulty. It's dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I don't know if any of the technical assistants could help us on that on the next upcoming video clip. Your Honour, in terms of expediency I'll continue to move along because I am concerned with what was said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, can I confirm that you were able to clearly hear what was said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As for my statement, it coincides more or less with what is said here, but the only difference is that from Jezestica they attacked Ejub Golic before that and he asked for assistance from Nurif Rizvanovic so he went up there to help. And one more thing, at Siljkovici, I didn't hear any special fighting but, well ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sometimes if the -- whoever is looking at the monitor changes position, either the position of the monitor or of himself or herself, you can actually see much clearer then. The same happens with our monitors. If you move them down, they -- whatever -- whatever you have on the monitor becomes clearer and less dark. So in the meantime, while the necessary adjustments are being made, the witness can be addressed to try and do that. Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this part of the interpretation is obviously not good. In the interpretation, I would like this to be played gone to the witness. What is said is "groups with Nurif Rizvanovic." However, in the Bosnian original, the person speaking says, "Led by Nurif Rizvanovic," which is something quite different. The interpretation of this part is rather poor. That's why I would like the witness to hear again what is said in the clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The entire clip or part of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The part where Nurif Rizvanovic is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's try and locate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, prior to doing that, can we just ask the assistance of the usher to see if his screen is adjusted so that it's visible to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Then I think if the monitor that he has is not adjustable, I think he himself has to move either nearer, see if you can -- by moving nearer, you can have a better -- better view. Is it any better?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I suggest we start playing the clip. Therefore the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. All right. But in the meantime, he is seeing me on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "And then I remembered something else again. When we -- when we did this [unintelligible], on the same day as that, the units that were around Bljeceva and Cizmici and Pale and Glogova, that is the unit from Glogova, at that time there were already quite a lot of people from Glogova who were armed, they had the task that with the help of people from Konjevic Polje, Nurif Rizvanovic" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, please. Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, one could clearly hear "with the assistance of the people from Konjevic Polje, led by Nurif Rizvanovic, or rather headed by Nurif Rizvanovic, and not, "with Nurif Rizvanovic" as it has been interpreted here. Do you agree, Witness, that this is entirely different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I just might interject. I appreciate Ms. Vidovic helping us with the interpretation of that word, and the question has already been posed by Ms. Vidovic to the witness as to what was his understanding. The Prosecution certainly will state that if that is the case, we have no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have any problem either, if that is the case; but we are in the in a position to confirm. But it seems that the witness does agree with Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's -- do we need to proceed further with -- I don't think we need to proceed further with the --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- with the video clip so you can put your question, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you hear in the video clip and understand that group or persons from Pale and Bljeceva were tasked to help the people from Konjevic Polje and Glogova in the attack in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I've heard. However, I've already indicated that Ejub Golic had among his men some from Bljeceva and Pale. They were members of his group. During the attack involving Ejub Golic and Nurif Rizvanovic and their men, that some other groups had been joining their forces, this is something I have never heard before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would just ask you, do you recognise anyone on the video? I'm not completely clear about how clear your video was but did you recognise anyone on the video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that I haven't really recognised anyone. I did my best but I was unable to recognise anyone. It wasn't very clear, the footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now like to proceed with the next video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Ms. Sellers. Witness, try to adjust your position as much as you can by coming nearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "On hearing that -- on hearing that Nurif Rizvanovic -- yeah, couriers were sent on to the free territory of Srebrenica, that is when they had broken through the Chetnik ambush, when they had got to the local districts of Potocari, that is to the municipality of Srebrenica, that is before Nurif Rizvanovic had set off through the forest to get to Srebrenica. He contacted -- made contact via the radio station on Livade the radio station on Livade with Ejub Golic, that he would then come, and that the army should expect him up there. When the courier got there, we already parts of -- [unintelligible] some of the soldiers with him. And then when the courier told Ejub that Nurif had fallen into a Chetnik ambush, and that he had 400 fighters with him who had come from Tuzla, that they all had camouflage uniforms, they all had Kalashnikovs, they all had all [unintelligible] ammunition, and they had infantry weapons but they had the complete, full set of infantry weapons. He then had -- he then had [unintelligible] and so went around to -- so before -- they went around to attack [unintelligible], Jezestica. Okay, so before he went to attack Jezestica, he sent a courier to Mirhet [phoen] Halilovic --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask just a question or two on this part. Were you aware that Nurif Rizvanovic and his soldiers had gotten into the Potocari locale while preparing and while undertaking this attack to Jezestica, because of an ambush?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your testimony before certainly indicated to the Trial Chamber that you were unaware of any communication that Nurif Rizvanovic had brought with him from Tuzla. After looking at this clip would you allow for the possibility that Nurif Rizvanovic's group, himself, being well-equipped, had brought or had the use of communications materials during this attack in Jezestica? Would you allow for that possibility, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would not accept that simply because I know nothing about it. I know nothing about the communications-related matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could I then assume that because of your lack of knowledge of communication matters, you would not be able to comment on the several references to couriers going between Nurif Rizvanovic's group or soldiers and other groups within the Potocari region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I definitely don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or did you know of someone named Mirzet Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived yourself in Srebrenica after the fall of Konjevic Polje, did you ever hear anyone speak about a Mirsad [phoen] Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't ever. I can tell you that I was located at the entrance to Srebrenica, next to the UN compound there, and I did not really inquire about who was doing what where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, right now if I would be able to go to the next video clip with this witness?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir I ask you again to look at your screen and to adjust it if it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: " [Unintelligible] He said that before he carried out -- before he went to do this attack on Jeretica [phoen], he sent a courier to Senad Skobic [phoen], a courier to Senad Golubovic, that's S-e-n-a-d G-o-l-u-b-o-v-i-c. He had replaced Mirzet who had left to become the head of the military police. He had troops who had been in Pale, and he said that he was going to attack Jeretica and as many soldiers as he had, he should also send to attack. And that Nurif had fallen into an ambush and that they had to attack the [unintelligible] above. Given that these -- it wasn't very far away, it was close - excuse me - they got there very soon, after about an hour and a half or two hours, where Ejub carried out a very strong attack in the area of Jeretica and when Nurif in the same way attacked Siljkovici, but he wasn't able to take the whole hill because the top of the hill was very exposed. They got about halfway up and then they had to withdraw, and they had to withdraw back towards Konjevic Polje. But Ejub Golic, together with the help of Senad Golubovic and his fighters, succeeded in taking the line of Jeretica, carry out a lightning action and then return. In other words, what they do is they collect the arms and ammunition and they go back to where they were. There was no point in keeping that line, in holding that line. "How long is that story going to go on for? "That's the end of the story. I just wanted to say that this was happening on the same day that I took Zalazje. After that, Nurif again tried to break through and succeeded in coming with his troops, and then these troops were deployed according to the places where they lived. Some went to on the line at Likari some stayed with Ejub Golic, and Nurif Rizvanovic, seeing that how things were in town itself, that there was nothing there, returned to Konjevic Polje. And from Konjevic Polje, went to Kamenica, then from Kamenica, the Chetnik offensive started and we'll talk about that later. We'll talk about the arrest of Nurif and [unintelligible] Brdo --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you now, did you recognise anyone in the video or the voice of anyone in the video, if you take those two parts separately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that the man who is talking right there is Mr. Naser Oric, although I cannot be 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of or hear about a man called Senad Golubovic that's referred to in this video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree with me that the Potocari, Potocari and the Potocari locale, is near Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that close to Srebrenica, really, some five to six kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you also agree that Pale and Bljeceva are in that locale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got to know about Pale and Bljeceva only upon my arrival to Srebrenica, because I went up there in search for food for my family. They were with me. The two villages are not that close either, although they are in close proximity of each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also I'd like to ask you a question because I think I might have misled you. I talked about the attack on the same day as Zaluzje and I should have said Zalazje. Did you hear about an attack on the 8th of August in Zalazje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Srebrenica or possibly prior to that, did you also know that other places such as Susnjari, Orici, Ogosia [phoen] were in that locale in the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't understood your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it -- I'm certain it might have to do with my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we might, I would like to see if the witness could be given the map? I think that might assist us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm talking about Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's show the witness map D908, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you look at the map, if we put it on the ELMO, please? Thank you. And could you locate the towns that we are speaking of, Pale, Bljeceva, Gostilj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Slowly, Ms. Sellers. I think what needs to be done first is to zoom in the area of Srebrenica because these villages are not far away from there, in any case. So, yes, more or less, more or less we need to zoom in, but please move the map towards the left. Yeah, okay. Now you can zoom in and it will be better. Can you see Potocari over there to the north of Srebrenica? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Ms. Sellers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please mark Pale on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you mark Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Look at Potocari, sir, and move at 10 hours, yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply to say that, with this witness, we would object to him being led as far as locations are concerned, if the point is to show he knows where they are, and -- because surely that's the point of the exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's a good point, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the point of the exercise is just to show that they are in the locale of Potocari and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Then you don't need a witness for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but you put the questions along those lines, to establish where these places are on the map, in any case, when we could actually locate them ourselves. So let's get over with this exercise, Mr. Jones, and finish it and continue with the proper evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you find Pecista? I'm sorry, could you also mark Pecista on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And also I would ask you to mark Gostilj, G-o-s-t-i-l-j, Gostilj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then finally Lehovici 9.53.15, please.?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, sir, my question to you is that either at this time period in August of 1992 or after, when you moved to Srebrenica, were you aware that there were fighters that were coming from these towns, this area, in the locale of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know anything about this. I've already told you that in 1992, there was no communication whatsoever between Srebrenica and Konjevic Polje, and I didn't know of the existence of any fighters over there, whether there were any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you reached Srebrenica in 1993, did you on that occasion learn about fighters from Srebrenica, from these different areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that I didn't know about any fighters. I heard about the existence of some groups in Konjevic Polje but that was all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to have the witness be shown Prosecution -- well, first it has ERN number - it will be a new exhibit - 03721259. Your Honour, this is a list of soldiers for commendation from the Potocari Brigade. It's a list of soldiers for commendation from the Potocari Brigade. That's the title of the document. And it consists of numbered names of 51, plus additional names written in the document. It's signed by Brigade's record keeper, Nukic, Muhmed [phoen] or Mumed Nukic. And in addition it has several names that one could number up to 62.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you to look at this document, and you will note that some of the persons listed under this document have died, have been killed, and under the latest are persons who were killed in -- I believe in 1993. My question to you after looking at the document and seeing the list of different companies and groups can you still state that -- even upon moving to Srebrenica, that you did not hear of fighters coming from these different groups under the Potocari Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still claim that I didn't hear anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about Naser's men or boys or the group that Naser Oric led coming from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about Naser Oric, some definite information about him only in 1994, so the entire 1993 passed without me knowing of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that there were a group of fighters from Potocari or referred to as the Potocari group or Naser's group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite possible but I didn't know of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your experience as a military person, have you ever heard the term -- excuse me right now, we can take the document from the witness and I would ask for a P number, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, this document which consists of one typewritten page with some handwritten names and marks, and three, four pages typed, typewritten in English, being the translation of the Serbo-Croat version is being tendered and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P596, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P596. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I was about to ask you, in your experience as a military person, having served in the army, have you ever heard the term "war path" used before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it important during times of armed conflict to note down the members of the group or unit, brigade or company, who were present and those who were deceased because of actions, in your experience as a military person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is something that should be done where the conditions permit it, but based on the situation we were in, I don't think something like that could have been done. We did not simply have the circumstances in place for it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence? The interpreter didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, could you please repeat your last sentence because the interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that, the conditions permitting, such records can be kept. However, it was impossible for us to have something of the sort. These were very small groups and I don't believe that any records were really kept. Such records ought to be normally signed and a stamp should be affixed to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir you would agree that where conditions permit, records such as participation, deaths of soldiers, their belonging to groups, should be kept. That's your testimony, I believe. Right, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is something that normally ought to be done but we did not have the circumstances permitting us to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under normal circumstances, would some person or persons be assigned to keep such records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, maybe you misunderstood my question. Under normal circumstances, would someone, or a person, from a unit usually be assigned to keep such records, such personnel records, as to who belonged to a unit, who might have been deceased during an action?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: As I understand it, these questions are being asked in this witness's capacity as someone who merely did his military service. If the only question, really, which I understand Ms. Sellers to be legitimately putting is in the system of the JNA before the war, was this the practice, otherwise it's so general and so vague, I don't see how the witness can possibly answer. He's been very clear that this was impossible during the war. So I understand, and perhaps Ms. Sellers can clarify, this is before the war in the JNA, was this the practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would certainly appreciate the intervention by Defence counsel, but I think there is no reason, given this witness's testimony, that's testified about things during this war, who has testified about his experience during this war, his experience after this war, the accumulation of his military experience it allows him to look at different things during there war, whether it be artillery or whether it be what would be normal practice, not normal practice. My question goes in that vein and, no, I'm not relating this necessarily back to JNA practice, Your Honour. So I think the witness can answer the question. I'm merely confirming one of the answers he gave. I don't think he's confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the problem with the notion of normal practice. What does that refer to? If the witness has said that in his experience this was impossible during the war, then obviously it wasn't normal practice. So I don't understand what normal practice refers to. It's utterly vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: With the disbandment of the JNA, the creation of the Serbian Republic, basically, the circumstances, the situation was no longer normal. So you can barely speak of normal circumstances after that happened and when the war started.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness has indicated - excuse me - to us that he then became part of a military organisation that exercised normal practice. So therefore he might draw on that experience as he's been asked to draw on other experience on other things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's also told you that when that happened the circumstances were such that it would not permit any of this taking place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's why my question goes to the extent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, I don't know where it will lead you in any case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just asking, to the extent possible he would agree that that's something that should be done. And I believe that the witness has already confirmed that, number one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But to do that, because I think Mr. Jones's intervention was fit and proper. Basically, what would you expect the witness to understand by normal circumstances? Under normal circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because ultimately, normal circumstances in those circumstances, would have been the circumstances obtaining prior to the war, not during the war. During the war there were no normal circumstances. He's told you that the circumstances were such that they probably didn't even have paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he hasn't stated that they didn't have paper and I haven't asked him that, but what I would like to clarify then is that, if the question is normal circumstances they don't necessarily relate back to the JNA, okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can ask the witness that; you're perfectly entitled to. But at the end of the day where's it going to take you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour at the end of the day I hope it takes me to a vital point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said it would be correct to take different records and different notes and you also testified that in your circumstances in Konjevic Polje that you were unaware that this occurred. Am I correct in that characterisation of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I listened to your questions and to His Honour and everybody else, and my conclusion is as follows: If you're asking me about my experience in the JNA, yes, of course, this was kept. If you're asking me about the war in 1992, and onwards, the conditions did not exist, not to mention paper. We had nothing at our disposal that would enable us to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would allow for the possibility that other groups who were fighting might have attempted to keep records of who was killed in action, soldiers who were killed in action, persons who belonged to units or persons who were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't learn anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question is -- has another connotation. Would you exclude that possibility? This is what ultimately Ms. Sellers wants from you. Granted that as far as you are concerned and your group is concerned, you are not in a position to do this, would you concede that it might have been possible with regard to other groups? This is what she is asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I know, the other groups were similar to mine. In other words, it would have been impossible to keep records on the entire territory of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. He's back to you, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, one of the important details that might be kept during wartime would be the different attacks or the different defensive mechanisms that a group or unit participated in. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you very well. Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly, certainly. One of the important types of records to keep or information to keep during a war would be the different attacks or defensive actions that a group or unit participated in. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you because we didn't have the conditions to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say, "we," you're referring to Konjevic Polje, that group, correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, you don't exclude the possibility that other groups might have had at least the conditions to keep some of that information on a recorded basis or to write it down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't say that, no, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To me, this is not a clear answer. What do you mean by saying "no, I wouldn't say that, no"? Do you exclude the possibility or do you concede that there could be possibly other groups that could -- that operated in conditions where they could keep such information on record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I don't know, I exclude it from my knowledge entirely. I don't know that they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think that's clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's fine. I would like the witness to be shown document ERN number 03720964. If it could be placed on the ELMO this time, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you to look over the document, and for the record I'll state that it is a document of two pages, on the back side of the first page we have writing in Cyrillic on there. It is a typed document entitled, "War path of Potocari Brigade, more important dates." Sir, I would ask you to look down at the different dates and under the 1st of June 1992, do you see the name of Ejub Golic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going further down where it says, 8th of August 1992, the first time it says 8th of August 1992, it says, "Action, Andrici, Jezestica, unsuccessful." Does the -- sir, would you state for the record whether you see that or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, does this coincide with your testimony in part that Jezestica on the 8th of August was the scene of combat activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, also, you've testified that on the 7th of January, that there was other actions, combat actions, in Jezestica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also, would you look further down where it says the 8th of August, 1992, just two entries down from the previous one, where it says, "Sabotage in Zaluzje and transport vehicle destroyed."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, sir, did you -- does this confirm what we've heard on the videotape about the attacks on the 8th of August, included Jezestica action, Andrici and Zaluzje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already told you that Zaluzje and the area up there was very far away, and I knew nothing about it. As for Jezestica, I said that the fighting up there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat, please, because the interpreter did not hear the last word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, the interpreters didn't catch the last part of your reply. You said "as for Jezestica, I said that the fighting up there," and then you said something else which they couldn't follow. What was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said about Jezestica, Your Honour, that I heard fighting up there, and when Nurif's fighters returned, this was confirmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Zaluzje was not mentioned at all on the video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think what was mentioned in the video clip was Zalazje and not Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I stand corrected. I understand that, because I even made a point of it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic is correct. These are two different places, Zalazje being the one which had great strategic importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir I would just ask you to go over to the second page and you see, under the 7th of January, what is legible action in Kravica. Does this coincide with your testimony that there was combat activity on the 7th of January 1993 in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was combat activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, I would ask you to note that on the dates of the 9th of May, the 27th of May, and on the 16th to the 20th of January 1993, the term "cleansing" is used. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what would "cleansing" mean in a military sense in relationship to these actions, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could correct what you said, the 9th of May, no, it was the 9th of March. Unless it was misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, on the document that I have it says page 2, I have 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It may have been a misinterpretation, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 9th of May, and I think you have to go also 27th of May, and then on the next page, it is -- I lost that. It's from the 16th to 20th, I suppose, of January, again, cleansing of the region, whatever it was. But you're being asked to explain the meaning of "cleansing," which occurs also in the part dealing with the 14th, 15th, and 16th of December, regards cleansing of Voljavica, Bjelovac, Kunjarac, Sase, Andrici. What do you understand, if at all, by the term "cleansing" in military terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as regards the word "cleansing", cleansing of the territory, liberating the territory, to make it free, but I don't agree that I should comment on this because I'm not familiar with that territory. This was in Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not being asked to comment on the events as such. You're just being asked to tell us whether you are familiar with the term "cleansing" and what you understand by it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cleansing of the territory in the area, the word speaks for itself in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a question with regard to language. I think the Bosnian term is [B/C/S spoken], [B/C/S spoken]. Now, this term, [B/C/S spoken], is it also used when people talk of ethnic cleansing or would you use in your own language a different term?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know whether one can speak of ethnic cleansing here. There is some kind of cleansing, but what kind of cleansing, I really couldn't explain in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think he's understood you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I think you did not completely understand my question. I guess you are aware that [unintelligible] it's not the question now -- that there has been ethnic cleansing in Bosnia-Herzegovina in those years. Now, if you would speak of ethnic cleansing, would you use the same term as is used here in terms -- sense of [B/C/S spoken] or would you have a different term? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no other word, only the word that's written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I'm afraid that that last answer is bound to be confusing. Obviously there is one word for cleansing, but the word for ethnic cleansing is obviously ethnic cleansing, and otherwise it might be understood that cleansing means ethnic cleansing. I hope that's not the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe that was in any way my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no, it was never the suggestion. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I mean, you don't need to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask for a P number for this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers. This will become Prosecution Exhibit P597 and it consists of a -- one-page in the Bosnian and Bosnian language and one handwritten page and then two typewritten pages, all of which are translated into English, the English text consisting of three pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying to move rapidly through this and I would ask that now the witness be shown the next document, and that's with ERN number 04231845. Your Honour, this is a document that is handwritten. It consists of 54 pages, of which on the last page there is not -- does not appear to be handwriting. I'm referring to it for convenience sake as a type of military diary, although I do not state for the record that that is the title of this document. I would also like to state that in the B/C/S, this document appears to start in the middle of a page and that, if Your Honours also look closely, there seems to be several different individual handwriting on the page and it appears to have been written on some form of a notebook.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I have a couple of questions I would like to ask you in relationship to things in this document. On the first page, at the top, the first page of B/C/S, there is a name that says, "Zakir Salilovic [phoen]" And next to it, it says, "Zenga".

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour if we could have this placed on the ELMO, it might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's place the English text on the ELMO, please. The top of the page, first four lines, is what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, wasn't it your testimony that some of soldiers who were with Nurif Rizvanovic were referred to as "Zengas" when they returned to Bosnia? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said nothing remotely similar to that. The question was, was the Croatian army known as the Zengas? That's what the witness was talking about. There was no mention of Nurif's men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. No it was in relation to some of Nurif Rizvanovic's men. In fact -- we can ask, we can go to the transcript and he was asked with regard to the ex-Croat component in his army, how they were known, and he referred to them as Zengas. So we can, without any problems, if you can find the transcript, easily, we can go back to this part of his testimony and refresh his memory. Do you have the quick reference, Ms. Vidovic -- Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did have it marked. Permit me one sec.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I found a reference here, it's on the 23rd of November and it's page 17, line 14, "Witness, the people who belonged to the Croatian armed forces before the outbreak of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, were they known under the name of 'Zenga'?" "Yes. I heard them being called Zengas on several occasions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but then he continues to speak about the components, of the Croatian component in Nurif Rizvanovic's group. He even specified the number roughly of ex-combatants from Croatia and then listed without naming combatants from Konjevic Polje. He did go through, but let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's the reference I have on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not waste for time on this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rizvanovic, I'm sorry that's not the name -- sir, could you just confirm, yes or no, that soldiers that came from Nurif Rizvanovic's group, who came from Croatia, you can confirm that they were referred to as "Zenga" at times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listening to these comments, I think I didn't mention Zengas in connection with Nurif Rizvanovic, but I did say that there was a Croatian army, the HVO, and the HOS. That's what I mentioned. I may have said that there were Zengas with Nurif Rizvanovic but you can check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not waste more time. He testified on these when he was shown the photos of one particular soldier with the Croatian army coat of arms and that he was part of Rizvanovic's group and he testified on that. But let's stick to what is relevant, Ms. Sellers, and move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We will move on. That was a relevant part as Your Honours will see in the future. I would ask now that the witness go to what is page 10 in the B/C/S version. And it's page 9 in the English -- I'm sorry, page 5 in the English version. And I want to point out where on page 5 in the English version it says, "company" and then it says "illegible," the name of the company is hard to decipher. And then I would ask now that we would go to page 10 in the English version, which is at the end of this section. And, Your Honour, it's page 15 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, I would draw your attention to the last line prior to the heading, "Meeting held on 19th of October 1994." And on that last line it says, "Until 16 October 1992, TO Potocari, our unit had the name, company Pecista." Do you see that line, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would ask you to go to page 11 in the B/C/S, which is in the same section of this last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And Your Honours it is page 7 in the English. And it's designated, I'll begin where it says "number 7." There it says --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, have you been able to locate that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "After the arrival of the army from Tuzla, on the 6th of August 1992, that army was distributed in our unit and with the units of Gostilj and Dugazi [phoen]. Conditions have been reached for forming a battalion of Gostilj. Pasalic Salih was appointed for the commander of the battalion. Osmanovic, Haris was appointed for the commander of the company Gostilj. Commander of the unit Pecista was Sinanovic Zunez [phoen], and commander of the independent battalion Dugazi was Besic Djosef Sruja [phoen]." Sir, does this confirm -- conform with your testimony that soldiers from Nurif Rizvanovic's unit then were placed in other units or other fighting groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have told you, I knew about -- about 10 men with Ejub Golic. As for the others, I really didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like you to look at number 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And it will be my last question, Your Honour, before the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right under it, and under number 8 it says, "unsuccessful action, Andrici. From 8th August 1992 there were 50 soldiers participating in this action, one soldier Ahmetovic, Ermin [phoen] got killed. There were three soldiers wounded and one of them heavily by stepping on to a mine." Sir, I would just ask you: Does this conform to any of your knowledge about a combat action in Andrici on the 8th of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know that this corresponds with Jezestica. As to Sandici I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you mean to say Andrici or Sandici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Andrici, excuse me, with Andrici. I don't know about Andrici; I do know about Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. I will stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you finished with this document or not yet?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we'll give it a number when we come back. May I ask you to cooperate and have a restricted break, 25 minutes, not 30?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, my Senior Legal Officer will approach you for the meeting now. With him he will approach you later on to fix a meeting with you, to discuss the future of the case. And let's hope that you will come up with practical solutions. The other thing I am told you wanted to know, whether we will be sitting on Wednesday. We won't be sitting on Wednesday, so we'll try to finish with this witness between today and tomorrow. See if the witness has a problem. He's not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't have any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That might pose a problem then for the next witness, the estimate is three and a half hours to four hours. I think I can safely say that I will be no more than three and a half hours. But nonetheless if I have only even let's say half an hour today and three hours tomorrow, I doubt the Prosecution will undertake to cross-examine in only 45 minutes. So if we -- and there are real problems with bringing the witness back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who will be dealing, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And how much time do you think you would require?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I anticipate the same amount of time although I haven't heard the testimony as of yet. So I can only say at first glance that I'll probably need the same amount of time, though, based on what the summary provided to us, I may be much shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not prepared to take risks of keeping the witness, then, here in The Hague until Monday, the 5th. If that is the case, we'll send him home, we'll bring him at some later point in time. Unless you agree to -- how much more time do you need, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I informed Madam Vidovic during the break I was going to definitely finish with this witness within the next session. I was hoping possibly a half hour to 45 minutes. I think that Mr. Jones would have more than a half hour with the witness today. That's my intention. Of course, the best-laid plans of mice and men ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Still, if he needs three and a half hours or three hours that would practically take the entire sitting of tomorrow. Let's say it will take first session and half of the second. It would leave about an hour, an hour 15 minutes, for the Prosecution for cross-examination. If you are prepared to decide now to split the time in a manner which would be agreeable to both, yes, we can proceed, otherwise, I don't know, I have no solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I just say, Your Honour, this is where it's so important that time estimates are stuck to, because we -- it was indicated to us on Friday that Ms. Sellers would finish by the first break. I've proofed the witness now for three days on the understanding that, of course, we would be finished by the first break and I would have the second break and the third session and I would have finished early tomorrow. There would have been plenty of time for cross-examination; everything would have been fine. And that's why we do have the impression from the Prosecution that they make time estimates which do not bear any resemblance to reality. And if we have to send this witness back, we're not going to be able to bring him back before Christmas because we have all the other witnesses lined up. It's a real -- real problem for us and I really had hoped that the Prosecution would be able to stick to -- stick to the time limit, and I anticipate, perhaps I'm wrong, but Ms. Sellers will say that there were objections which slowed things down. Well, if objections are valid, then that has to be factored into the time which it takes to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sellers, can you finish in 30 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think 30 minutes to 45 minutes with already setting aside some evidence that we thought was crucial to present, and I think in terms of factoring in objections. And I agree with Mr. Jones that there has been quite a bit of oral litigation during the presentation of this witness. I disagree that that has been a factor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There hasn't been.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: One half hour of my presentation on Friday was devoted to oral arguments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's continue and we see where we get to and, if necessary, we will send the witness home and tomorrow we will deal with the Rule 68 bis matters, instead. We will see. Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we are going to continue with the document we had before. I would ask you to turn to page 29 in the B/C/S. And in the English it is page 22. On page 22, you see that one-third, one-quarter of the way down the page, it says, "Company, Susnjari." I would then ask that you turn to page 30. In the English, we are now on page 23. At the bottom of the English page, it says, "Jezestica, on the 8th of August 1992, 65 soldiers participated with weapons, one M53, two PM, 12 automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles, five, 8 Gar. [phoen], one drummer machine-gun, one sniper, ten LPs, six old fashioned pistols," and there is a bit that's illegible. "The rest of them were without weapons. The action was successful, burnt completely, seized one M53, one LP, there were six wounded soldiers on our side and five were killed on mines. One case of ammunition, M53, and 200 pieces of 7.62 millimetre ammunition, five Chetniks were killed. One group was led by Sudek [phoen], and the other by Valagin [phoen]." Sir, again I pose the question to you: Does this conform with your knowledge that there was an attack in Jezestica on the 8th of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I can anticipate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The answer is bound to be misleading. The witness has said that there was an attack. That's fine. Whether this conforms with his knowledge by that means Ms Sellers means to get in all the rest of it, which he hasn't confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, did I not ask him to confirm the rest of it. I asked him to just confirm to his knowledge that there was an attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's already confirmed before that there was an attack in Jezestica on the 8th of August. He said it. I haven't counted the times he did confirm that so why do you want him to confirm it again?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: If he's able to Your Honour, for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: If not, I'll move on to another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then ask him whether he confirms once more that there was an attack on Jezestica on -- because otherwise, Mr. Jones is completely right. I mean, you've read out six, seven lines here giving a lot of details, and then you ask whether this conforms with his statement, prior statement, that there was an attack on Jezestica. Bottom line would be later on, you would say, you would bring that as an argument in favour of the authenticity or probative value of this document and what it contains. I mean, it's -- and I think you understand me 100 per cent well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand you 100 per cent well. And given that guidance, I can certainly allow us to move a bit more rapidly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, then I would just ask you one question in terms of the part that I've just read out, is it still your testimony that you were unaware that there was burning at -- during the attack in Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would then -- I now ask that this document be given a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document in the original Serbo-Croat version is entirely handwritten. It starts with ERN number 04231845 and goes through and up to 04231872 -- 72. And then it's followed by a typed translation of it in English, consisting of 44 pages, typed pages, with the same ERN range of numbers. Yes, Ms. -- this document is being entered and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P598. Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I noticed a while ago something that I would wish to draw your attention to which is the Rule 90(H)(ii) provision. We had a witness here who had direct knowledge of the events in Susnjari concerning the group. In accordance with Rule 90(H)(ii), the Prosecutor was duty-bound to put his case or her case to the witness and ask him about the specific events contained herein. The Prosecutor did not do it at the time but instead does it in relation to this witness, who has no knowledge, but to indirectly confirm the authenticity of this particular document. I believe that the Prosecutor just as we are, is duty-bound to comply with the provisions under Rule 90(H)(ii), and this course of proceeding constitutes a direct violation thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you notice, this witness's testimony went to the attack on Jezestica and that I'm going through various geographical groups or units that might have participated in it. In terms of this document having been presented to the other witness, I would like to not divulge too much work product but, Your Honour, in terms of translation, in terms of analysis of Prosecution exhibits, they are not necessarily available at the time that certain witnesses come. I think Your Honours might certainly recognise that we are asking for a P number for this document today and have not used it with any preceding witnesses although that we might have had witnesses that were testifying about different things that could be relevant to the document. So there has been no violation of Rule 90(H) unless the Prosecution is duty-bound to anticipate all evidence. I think that if a violation according to Madam Vidovic has been made it's certainly not been made in any type of bad faith, and that this witness has been asked to respond to what he could testify against. And if he could not, he clearly indicated to the Trial Chamber his lack of knowledge thereof.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am truly surprised. This document was in their possession not only in advance of the testimony of this witness but of another witness as well. I will file a written filing concerning this. I do not think it is really proper for the -- my learned colleagues to say something that is contrary to the truth. You had this document at the time when the Susnjari group leader testified. There were even a couple of questions put to him concerning this. I, in fact, anticipated at the time that you would proceed the way you proceeded right now, that you would not confront that particular witness with this document, but would rather wait to confront a different witness with the same paper. I would kindly call on my colleagues to comply with the provisions of the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect I think that the last portion or one portion of my presentation is not just possession but it was analysis of the document, and I said I do not want to go into work product at that time, but the Prosecution certainly reserves the right prior to using a document to analyse it from its point of view. And I think that that is what Madam Vidovic has not taken into account in her later argument. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Would you be following this up with a proper motion or shall we move ahead, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, if I may, Your Honour, the whole issue of 90(H)(ii) is something we are going to definitely place great emphasis on at some point in submissions. I won't undertake now to file on this specific issue within a specific time, but it's a matter of great concern to us that the documents and propositions are not being put to witnesses to whom they should be put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll come to that even when we are seized again with it. For the time being we'll move ahead. We will discuss amongst ourselves and, if we need to come back to you on this, we will. In the meantime we will, of course, keep what you have submitted in our minds. Yes, Ms. Sellers, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like the witness now to be shown document with -- the ERN number is 02116725. Your Honour, for purposes this is a document that relates to the TO Gostilj Srebrenica. It has a P number following the location. It appears to be a series of names and members of that unit. It goes to number 76. It's a handwritten document, and the Prosecution has submitted a translation and one will note that the translation is a partial translation that allows those who are English speakers to understand what are the headings of the different columns and some of the functions attached to the names in the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, my question is the following: In the previous document, remember there was a portion that related to some of Nurif Rizvanovic's troops being placed in different units, different groups, including the group of Gostilj. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember saying that there was -- that there was only Ejub Golic's group. I don't remember any other groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question was that in the previous document that we saw, there was one portion that talked about the group of Gostilj and how it too would receive soldiers, persons, from Nurif Rizvanovic's group. Do you remember that portion, the previous document, that's my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would draw your attention to number 19 on this list and number 19 gives the name of an Azmir Midzic [phoen] - if I'm pronouncing this correctly - and I would ask to you go over -- well, I'll wait until you find that. I believe it's on the first page, number 19, three up from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't read it Mrgzic [phoen], I read it Merizic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Merizic. Merdzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Merdzic, M-e-r-d-z-i-c

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go over to the column that says --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Joined TO" and follow that down to the person's name, I'm wondering could this be placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The B/C/S version, Ms. Sellers? Because if you put the English version, it doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I think the B/C/S version is a bit more illustrative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Mr. Jones, please, your microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, if you go over to the column where it says, "joined the TO," do you see 6-08-92, meaning August 6, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 14th of August? Yes, I have it. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, and then would you please go over three more columns where it says 06-08-92?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if the usher could assist, we are still on the first page, number 19 and I'm just asking him to go over columns on the line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm doing my best to try and find where Ms. Sellers can identify the 6th of August 1992 because here it says the 6th of June 1992. I think this is misleading to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I read it as you do, Ms. Vidovic. I don't see it 06-08-92. I see it 06-06. However, if we zoom in that area of the document, perhaps we can see it better. We are talking of four lines from the bottom of the screen now, and we need to zoom in in the third column starting from the right. To me it's still 06-06-92.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour. I'll withdraw the question. It appeared to be an 8 to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not saying that it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't -- I -- my impression is an 8. In trying to follow through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, I will withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you look at the last -- one but last column where you have those two-digit numbers plus a letter and you look at the 8 that is written there, 81, 82, 83, et cetera. There is no way you can say that the previous column 06, the next would be 08. To mean it's 06-06-92. There is no similarity between that second digit in the middle with the 8 that show us up in the penultimate column. I may be wrong. I don't want --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't belabour the point, because I certainly think that it's a possibility that that's an 8, in comparing even to the handwriting in the last column, whether that was made slightly different. But I will withdraw the question from the witness. I do not intend to try and mislead the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. I'm sure you were not trying to mislead the witness but -- okay, let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, I would also ask to you look at this document under the second column, meaning where the names are, and starting with number 1, 2 and 3, do you see the functions of persons under the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under line number 3, do you see the function that says, "Guard commander"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then on 4 through 23, do you see the function that says, "Soldier"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, he's to remain on the same page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on number 24, do you see the designation that says, "Soldier, quartermaster"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell Your Honours what would be a quartermaster in your experience in the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quartermaster's service is supposed to perform its duties in the rear, as part of the logistic support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, if you would continue down to number 28, do you see the word, "Courier"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
