utterances.text: And then afterwards, on 29 and 30, do you see the word "cook"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you to go to the two names next to cook and could you confirm for the Trial Chamber whether those are the names of women or the names of moan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are female names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, May i just say, and I don't know if the witness has been tested on his eyesight or his ability to read what's in front of him. I don't know if there are any meaningful questions which the -- Ms. Sellers actually has for this witness about this document, or whether we just have an extended submission or demonstration for Your Honours which really is a matter of submission. I've been listening for the last five minutes to see if there is a meaningful question for this witness which he can tell us about TO Gostilj and people here, and there isn't. It's simply, do you see this, do you see that, and I really -- particularly when we are so short of time I despair a bit that we are going to lease so much time when there is no meaningful question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would rather wait, Mr. Jones, and see what would be the final question on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, sir, I would ask you to look at number 31, and that goes down through, I believe, number 39, where the word "guard" is listed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the testimony that you've given us before, you've testified that in your area that persons acted as guards to guard the front line; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you have considered those guards, persons who functioned as guards, as part of the groups that you had in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the group in my village, that is, the question you put before, not soldiers but armed men who were defending their villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, in the list that we've gone through, you've noticed that there are couriers, a courier has been listed. Now, you've testified that you didn't know about couriers or you didn't have any couriers in your group. If there had been couriers in your group, would that be a normal function or would that be a military function within fighting groups or units?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be unusual to have couriers in groups in order to take messages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be unusual if it was in the military sense. As this was not in the military sense because these were groups defending their hearth and home and their children. In my group there were no couriers. But if there was an attack launched by the other side there had to be people who would go and ask for assistance, to help defend the territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those people might be referred to as couriers; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. You misunderstood this. You have completely misunderstood this. You keep talking about couriers, but if a courier is someone who is at the line and he has to run and tell someone something urgently, he's not a courier. He has to abandon his position on the line in order to go and run to ask for assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. So there is a difference between people who run for help and people who would take messages as a courier. As I understand, that's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's clarified now. And I would just have one other question concerning this document, and, sir, at the very beginning of the document, under number 3 there is a guard commander. Do you know what the function of a guard commander would be in a unit or in a fighting group?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, I think we have to talk about whether this is the JNA we are talking about or in some theoretical concept which the witness is asked to imagine. I mean surely the witness has a right to have concrete questions put to him. What unit, what fighting group, when, where?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you speak of a guard commander, because I am not familiar with military structures as some of you might be, would this be something which is universal? A guard commander? Or is it something that is particular to the -- I don't know, to the armed forces, ex-Yugoslavia? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is precisely part of the nature of my question. We see this here, the witness has testified about certain military matters, and I see this function "guard commander." He's also testified about having worked in the border service, about guards, having guards within Konjevic Polje, and I just felt that he would be in a position to allow us possibly to understand guard commander as contained in this document. That certainly is about a unit in a geographical location that we've already discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then ask him whether he's familiar with the term guard commander in a military context, and what he understands with that term, and any other question that may arise out of that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And since Gostilj -- since Ms. Sellers said it's about this document, the guard commander fled to here, he should be asked whether Gostilj TO, whether he understands what was meant in that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's already stated that he never heard of Gostilj TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's why this exercise is so useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would, I would --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Defence counsel would continue through -- in front of this witness, I believe try and align the questions that he's being asked, I think it's unproductive in terms of the testimony this witness can give. The question I asked I believe it has now gone up on the monitor was precisely in the nature of what Your Honour put forward of what is a -- what is a guard commander. I believe I asked "if in a unit." In the military context what could be a guard commander. If we would not have a characterisation of a question to that extent prior to the witness responding, I think it would be much more helpful timewise and evidentiary wise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you assist the Trial Chamber, if you know, of what a guard commander could be in the military context [microphone not activated] unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military context, a guard commander or a guard shift leader is someone who is in charge of the guard and takes the guards' shift to their post. That's in peacetime. However, in these wartime conditions, if you're asking me about that, to be a guard -- to be a leader of a group in those areas, the leaders of those groups didn't have -- didn't command really. They had guards in those places where I was in wartime conditions. And they themselves stood guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that a P number be attributed to this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers, this document which consists of four pages, handwritten pages in B/C/S, with ERN 02116725 to and inclusive of 6728, and in English -- reproduction in English of the template used for the B/C/S version together with a reference to particular numbers, and duty description is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit P -- as Prosecution Exhibit P599.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now just like to show the witness a video clip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to showing this video clip, Witness, I -- sorry, I would just like to remind you that you stated that prior to Nurif Rizvanovic coming, that the fighters in or the men in your area, Konjevic Polje, didn't have uniforms. Now, is it your testimony that with the coming of Nurif Rizvanovic that uniforms were finally distributed or worn or distributed to fighters within the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who could distribute the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did the fighters start wearing -- some fighters start wearing uniforms at that time period? Wasn't that your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that anyone wore a uniform. There was no one to distribute uniforms. They only brought the uniforms they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like you to watch this video, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are these similar to the times of uniforms that Nurif Rizvanovic's men wore or that were worn by his men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These uniforms are similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We'll continue now nor a second.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the person who is on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Mr. Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell Your Honours what he appears to be wearing on his left shoulder, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that he has some sort of insignia here but you can't see precisely what the insignia is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he also appear to be carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't see any weapon here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We'll continue now with the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you look at the two men in uniforms now pictured on the screen? And my question to you is, the patch on the man's arm that is standing up near what appears to be a window, is that a patch that you described earlier as belonging to the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, we are at 07.186.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, it could be the patch of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina but you can't really see it very clearly or in any detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the man that's now pictured in the video? I will ask you first do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, before you answer, we are at 07.259. It's very dark. I agree. I can barely see the face.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand. The screen I'm looking at is much brighter than the screen that's appearing on Sanction. I would ask the usher would you just verify the screen the witness has? Maybe we'll have to tilt it and I would certainly like him to see as clear an image as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The same applies with me. I mean, Judge Eser's is less dark than mine. You know, it's --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask to you look at the person, if you can, pictured on the screen now, and first, could you tell me whether you know this person or not, you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see it at all here. It's so dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to see an insignia on the person's hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see that either. You can come and look for yourself, if you like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree that I cannot approach you right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the technical difficulty is unfortunate for the Prosecution's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't help you, Ms. Sellers. I mean, we've gone through this, and I think, to be honest with you, we can jump to something else because we went --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- through this video already with someone else and we've received testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: As it pertained to this witness, we didn't. I will now move to my final video. And let's hope that there will be a little light shed on the image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the image on your screen now, the video, with enough light in order to tell? First, let me ask you, do you recognise anyone in this video shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recognise anyone here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the uniforms that are in this video shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The uniforms are camouflage uniforms. You can see them on the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the types of uniforms that were worn by Nurif Rizvanovic's men when they came into the region in August 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ones like these or similar to these.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they ones like these or are they ones similar to these, sir? I didn't understand whether you were giving an answer or asking a question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said they were either like these or they were similar to these.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now draw your attention to the patch on the person's sleeve that appears to be on the right-hand side of the screen, the lower right-hand side. Would you agree that this is similar to the patch that you described coming from the ABiH on uniforms of Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It should be the same or should be similar; that's what you're saying, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We'll continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would just ask you, do you by any chance recognise any of the buildings that are in this video?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to state that those previous two films come from P433, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and we are at still point 59.138.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: To correct the record the previous video was Prosecution's Exhibit 318 and the last one is Prosecution Exhibit 433. I just have a couple of questions to finish up, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when Nurif Rizvanovic left the region, isn't it true that he had been arrested by Naser Oric and his men prior to eventually leaving the Konjevic Polje region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You couldn't really say that he was arrested by Naser Oric, but there was a rumour going around that he had been arrested. I've already said that. Another possibility was that he went off somewhere. There are many people in Konjevic Polje who don't know precisely whether he was arrested or whether he left of his own accord, but more people seem to be of the opinion that he just went off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware that Zulfo Tursunovic might have physically hit or in any other way physically attacked Nurif Rizvanovic's person prior to his going off after he had been arrested? Sorry, prior to his going off or leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you referred to Nurif Rizvanovic as a commander, someone who acted like a commander and someone who was respected as a commander. Correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He acted like a commander but he never agreed to have anyone respect him as a commander. Wherever he went, there were only those small groups, and that did not suit him at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he referred to other persons as commanders, such as Hakija Meholjic and people in the area; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that in 1994, that there was some kind of letters involving Hakija Meholjic because of some successes he had had in the liberation of Srebrenica. Srebrenica had been occupied territory before that. The first person to enter it in 1992 was Hakija Meholjic, with some kind of group of his. I'm not a hundred per cent sure of the correctness of this information but I'm telling you everything I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you agree that Nurif Rizvanovic being a commander himself would know how to recognise persons, other persons, who were commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, but I don't know exactly. Probably he would be able to recognise someone if that someone was a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, a couple last questions and hopefully we can pass through them very rapidly. You yourself never physically went to Jezestica during this time period, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you wouldn't know if there were any civilians, any elderly people, who might have still been in the town of Jezestica on the 8th of August 1992, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that one of the Eric brothers was physically disabled and couldn't move around very freely. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know whether he or other members of his family were still in Kravica on the 7th of January 1993 or whether he was able physically to get out, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could know a little bit about that with respect to the elder brother, Nego Eric, who couldn't move about freely. Some people who were next to that house told me that shots were fired from that house and what happened after that, I really wouldn't be able to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he died in the house with his wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you I didn't know what happened next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, lastly, I would like to ask you, do you know what happened to Kostadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about Konstantin [as interpreted] Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he survived the war or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the man. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can redact it without any problems but anyway, let's not argue about it. Let's redact page 57, lines 2 to 11. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, then my last question is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we understand that there will be a time period when you're going to be asking for retirement benefits and?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I don't know whether it would be preferable to have this in closed session or not. I don't know how identifying that would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To play it safe, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not at the time, Your Honour. Re-examined by Ms. Vidovic: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness I believe P559 has been given to you which is a document concerning the proposal for a medal for Mr. Munib Sabic. In connection with this, to your knowledge, is it at all true that in the area of enclave before the fall of Srebrenica, there was a practice in place to award medals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, have you ever heard that Munib -- of Munib Sabic being nominated to be awarded any medal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm sure that nothing of the sort ever existed because I attended his funeral.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with Munib Sabic and the document, I will ask you as follows: Have you ever seen this document, P559 -- 595? It has been shown to you. According to this document, Munib Sabic has turned the tide of the fighting on the 29th of May 1995. Is it true at all that it was Munib Sabic who had turned the tide of fighting on the 29th of May 1992 or was it actually done by a group of people who came in to help you in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. It was this group of men who arrived to our aid who turned the tide to our favour and not Munib who helped us -- me with the bottley [phoen] devices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is stated that Munib Sabic had an automatic rifle, is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it at all true that on the 29th of May 1992, he himself managed to kill eight Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will show you another document, D804. Could the witness please be given D804? And while this is being done, please listen to my question carefully. Look at the document before you related to Munib Sabic or you don't even have to. It is stated "On the 17th of December 1992, when our fighters returned, and this time they were not successful, in -- on the Kravica front line, the person who became leader and led them to Donja Branakuslj [phoen] and Banjevici, when the above-mentioned Chetnik strongholds were captured and several Chetniks were placed hors de combat." Please look now at D804. This is a document by the command of the Bratunac Brigade dated 18 December 1992. This is therefore the report drafted the following day, which says that the village of Krusik was attacked, and that the Serbs had been pushed away from there. Please, therefore, look at the document dated 18 December and look at paragraph 2, wherein it is stated, "They discussed the Serbian line and it says, "From the Drina River to the Tosici hill," and so on. Look at sentence two, "From the top of Avdagina Njive behind the village of Bozici, Mocila, Djermani, Siljkovici, Doljani and the village of Krusik." Do you agree with me that this particular document issued by the Bratunac Brigade says that the Serbian line was in the village of Krusik on the 17th [as interpreted] of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of the Muslim forces or Muslim groups or Muslim armed men, whichever way you like it, attacked Banjevici and defended Bacici on the 17th of December 1992, have they ever done that before mid-January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Throughout my testimony, I believe I related things as they had happened, and I'm sure, I'm positive, that the things did not happen this way as stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday the Prosecutor suggested to you whether perhaps the information concerning Munib Sabic had been a bit exaggerated. My question to you is as follows: What is stated in this document, is it at all true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Munib Sabic was not an armed man and he definitely did not attack anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Noticed you standing for the last minute or so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's a bit confusing, the transcript, when I believe the witness is referring to a document, and I don't know whether he's referring to the document that Madam Vidovic has just presented from the Drina Corps, whether he's referring to the document referring to the medals. He says it's not true what's in the document, and I just wanted to ask could we have that clarified for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that needs to be clarified. Are we talking of document P595 or this document, D8 -- I missed the number now. 804.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am referring, of course, to this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when I asked you to confirm the accuracy of the document, I meant the one speaking about the alleged medal awarded to Mr. Munib Sabic, or rather, P595. And my question was whether the contents of the document were accurate, be it with regard to Munib Sabic's medal or to the attack taking place against the village of Krusik, the radio set there, taking place on the 17th of December 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither of these are true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would not want the witness to be misled. The document that the Prosecution presented regard to medals were proposals. It is nothing about, I think, Madam Vidovic said the alleged awarding of. There is nothing in the document that says the medals were awarded. These were proposals that were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, correct, too. But we still -- we are not actually I know what you've just mentioned is important but basically what Ms. Vidovic is addressing is the contents of the basic information for the proposal, proposed -- for the proposal itself. Anyway, let's move. Let's move. Let's move ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you were quite clear that I referred to the contends of the document concerning the proposed award of medals. In connection with this, have you ever heard of Munib having been proposed to receive such a medal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a minor matter to mention. The other document I was mentioning, D804, is dated 18 December 1992, and my questions had to do with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I'm following the English, obviously. It's just to say that in page 60, line 11, it was wrongly recorded 17th of December 1992. My learned colleague's question was: Is it correct that the line -- the Serb line went through Kruscic on the 18th of December 1992. It is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness now please be shown P596?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it says here, list of soldiers for commendation from the Potocari Brigade. Based on what you can see here, can you have any idea at all or make an inference as to the time period in which the document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document does not bear any date pointing to when it may have been drafted, nor does it have any stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P597?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at page 1. Do you agree with me that it's written in the Cyrillic and that in the Cyrillic it says "the war record of the Potocari Brigade," and then important data and then it is all written in the Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish to direct your attention to one date, where it says, on -- at the top, it says, "the war record of the Potocari Brigade, and then it says the 8th of August 1992, Jezestica action-unsuccessful." Based on what you know about it, can you tell the Trial Chamber whether Andrici and Jezestica are one and the same area, or is Andrici actually quite far away from Jezestica and the entire area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about Jezestica only upon my arrival in Srebrenica and I heard that they ARE quite far apart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That Andrici and Jezestica are quite far apart from each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, or rather the Prosecutor drew your attention to Ejub Golic. Based on what you know about Ejub Golic, had this man ever -- before the fall of Srebrenica had anything to do with the -- any of the units of the Potocari or the Potocari group itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In general terms, do you know anything about the events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers? You have an objection to the previous question, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, I had to wait for a translation, and just the phrase, "anything to do." That's quite broad, anything to do with the Potocari unit, and I don't know whether Madam Vidovic is referring to participating, participants, joint action, coordination, but the question appears to have been answered by the witness. I'm uncertain of his connotation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the witness understood my question and answered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, generally speaking, did you see, were you there, either the Andrici or the Jezestica action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was -- did not -- I wasn't there. I only heard about the Andrici action, whereas for the Jezestica action, I could hear the guns firing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any events in Zalazje in the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not hear anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that Zalazje is in an area quite separate from that of Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'll direct your attention to the -- to what is purported to be a war diary. Have you personally ever heard of any other group except for Ejub and Nurif's men having -- as having participated in the attack against Jezestica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear of any other groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at page 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 11 of which document? Of the same document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I took it for granted that the document -- no, P598.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a different document. What's the corresponding page in English, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's page 11 in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might assist, I think it's page 7 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, under number 8, it is stated, "the unsuccessful action of Andrici on the 8th of August 1992, 50 fighters took part in it," and so on and so forth. You replied to the Prosecutor's question and stated that this was -- conformed with Jezestica. Is it not true that the dates tally rather than the other information contained here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the weapons or the fighters who are report -- who reportedly took part in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with this, do you know what the Pecista company, if it ever existed, did in the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know who was doing what in Srebrenica. I only knew about the civilians who were always in search of bread.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't even aware of the existence of the Pecista company, let alone what it did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will put to you a series of questions in connection with what you were able to see in the video clips. First P328, where you said that you could not recognise the person who spoke. Do you remember the video clip you were shown, and, on the basis of what you heard, can you conclude which time period the person speaking has in mind? Does the person mention whether it's the August of 1992 or January 1993 or any sort of date that would allow you to place the statement by this person into a time frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The person never mentioned any date so I cannot really draw any inferences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard the person mentioning tasks. Were you able to understand on the basis of what the person was saying who was assigning the tasks the person mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not able to understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on what you could hear the person say, were you able to conclude whether the person referred to own experience or to something that the person had heard from someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my impression was that the person was referring to something the person had heard from someone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us at all whether you know if the person speaking had accurate information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a person who speaks Bosnian and/or Croatian/Serbian, were you able to hear the interpreter interpreting what the person was saying? Based on what -- on how the person speaks, can you conclude whether the person has a good command of Bosnian and/or Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the person spoke Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question did not have to do with the version but, rather, whether the person had a good command of the language. Were you able to understand the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. Not that well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last document shown to you -- and could the witness please be shown the document again, P599? First of all, the Prosecutor suggested that the document had to do with the Srebrenica TO. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the heading, the title. Does it say the list of members of the TO Gostilj-T-Srebrenica [as interpreted]? Do you agree with me that it doesn't say Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards Gostilj, do you have any knowledge of this unit, whether it existed, how it operated, how many men it had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know of any unit, and I mean in Gostilj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I just make a correction for the transcript? It said Gostilj P, not T. Line 21, 22:49, or, rather, line 12 and it should say TO Gostilj P-Srebrenica rather than T. Line 12, 22:49. By taking a glance at the document, can you infer who authored the document and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document does not contain any dates and I don't know if I can see who authored it, no, no. It doesn't say who authored the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have another question in relation to this document. Have you ever heard or rather had you ever heard prior to the demilitarisation, that there were any quartermasters or quartermaster services in the area of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I hadn't heard anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your arrival in Srebrenica, and after the fall of -- after the fall of Srebrenica, had you heard of the existence of any quartermaster services in the area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you as to the date that you indicated as having entered the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina for retirement purposes, and you said that it was the date of your arrival in Srebrenica. Can you tell the Trial Chamber when it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was in the month of March, perhaps the 12th or the 13th. I'm not sure. I didn't have a calendar at hand. But perhaps I can clarify in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, please just give us the date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they keep it in their records as of 1994, although this wasn't in fact the case. It was just formally put on paper as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser would like to put some questions to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, we talked a lot about Nurif Rizvanovic. Do you know whether he's still alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even nowadays, Your Honour, I hear that he is still alive, that his family is somewhere in Slovenia. Whether this is really the case, I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The next question: In the direct examination, asked by Madam Vidovic whether the groups in Konjevic Polje did accept Nurif Rizvanovic as a commander. You answered: At that time Bego Muminovic told me that he had been -- Rizvanovic, was accepted. Do you know how it came about that they accept him as commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came to Konjevic Polje, he said that his intention was to be commander of the Drina region. I cannot tell you really what the date of his arrival was, but they had a meeting which was attended by Bego Muminovic and that was when Nurif was accepted as commander of the Drina region. However, this was never really operational. He would sometimes criticise us, that we did not adhere to something that had been previously agreed, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, when Rizvanovic had left the area, some people stayed behind. Those people who stayed behind, where did they originate from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones who stayed behind, when Nurif Rizvanovic left, hailed from the municipality of Bratunac and they were under the command of Refik Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, with regard to Refik Hasanovic, he followed Rizvanovic as commander, and how did that happen that he was following Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this came to happen. They agreed amongst themselves, but later on, he wasn't commander of the Drina region but, rather, a commander of a company, because many things changed after Nurif Rizvanovic left. The numbers reduced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, you had testified that on the 27th of April 1992, there have been founded groups in Racanici [phoen] with Kadric as leader, and Pobrdje with Omerovic, that seemed to have happened at the same day. Was there a special reason for this, that it happened on the same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was established same day of the return from Sandici because we could see that there was a buildup of the Serb forces. We anticipated that they would attack us which was, in fact, the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So can I conclude that it was a reaction to what was going on on the Serb side that, on the Muslim side, you would try to form civil village guards and groups who could defend their villages? Is that a correct understanding of your -- of what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The groups were established after the men returned from Sandici, when Alija Osmanovic was slapped around. It was subsequent to that that the groups were established, but they were established independently of each other. It wasn't as if they said altogether that they were going it establish these groups. They established groups in -- separately in Okuvici [phoen] and in other places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: With regard to the event of the 29th of May, where you had this -- tried to block the road, and you had testified that quite -- you have been assisted from other groups. Now, how did it -- how did you get the help or how could -- did you inform the groups from outside of your own village to come to assist you? On what way was this information given?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, there have been people moving back and forth from one side to the other to transfer or transport certain information. Now, if you had to describe this type of getting information from one place to another place, how would you describe it, this sort of activity?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Judge Eser; let's redact again lines 7 to 10, please. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Witness, I didn't ask you now how it was done. I was more interested how you would describe this activity, but how you would name it, would you call these people bringing information from one place to another, could you call them messengers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D005 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call them messengers. They were people guarding the line and observing the Kravica area, because that's where attacks came from most frequently. It was the men on the line observing in that direction. They didn't have time to go back to the village and give a report and so on. They went straight to ask for assistance. For example, from Hrncici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But is it your opinion that to defend your own village would not be possible by doing it also by bringing messages from one place to the other, does the one activity exclude the other one? Wouldn't it be possible that defending the village could also mean that you act as a messenger between different places?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there is a misunderstanding, because this is the second time this witness has answered this question. We are probably familiar also in our own in English with runners. If you ever a system where you have people in the lines and then runners who take messages. This witness has said, "We didn't have messengers in that sense. There weren't runners designated to do that task. People would leave the line and run and take a message." And that's what he's saying. So I think there is some misunderstanding if it's being suggested to him that he's excluding that people took messages. He's given his evidence on this. I don't know if Your Honour wants him to accept that they were couriers or something like that. It seems that's what's being suggested to him. Surely he's explained the situation. Is it necessary to put words in his mouth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I think I have enough answer on it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So there are no further questions from the Bench which basically means that your testimony comes here -- comes to an end here. Sir, I wish to thank you so much on behalf of the Tribunal, on behalf of Judge Brydensholt, Judge Eser for having kindly come over to give testimony as a witness for the Defence. Yes, I recognise Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we forgot to ask the witness to sign the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Vidovic. Before you leave the courtroom, we need you to sign the map, Exhibit D908 -- 908, and, for that reason, that map will now be kept under seal, will now be kept under seal. Now, sir, you will soon be escorted out of the courtroom by Madam Usher and you will see all the assistance you require to facilitate your return back home at the earliest. Once more, I thank you, and I also wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the position -- yes, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I think to make use of the time it's worth me floating a suggestion which I hope Your Honours will consider a practical one. We really do think that after three days of proofing this witness, this witness who's travelled here, he's been waiting to testify --.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I'm thinking as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- that it would be a real shame if we couldn't find some way to finish his testimony. I've looked quickly at statistics for, certainly during the Prosecution case, how long we took as a percentage of the time for examination-in-chief, and it was approximately 75 per cent on average. We haven't been a hundred per cent of the time for the Prosecution on each occasion. And with those statistics in mind, and also with the suggestion that I'm certainly going to stick to what is relevant for the next witness, and he's testifying on something very specific concerning municipal staffs in Tuzla, if the Prosecution can do likewise and not seek to raise matters with the witness which he can't comment on and which are not relevant and which are not the area he knows about. If he's not asked to comment on TO Gostilj or something of that nature, then I suggest the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I certainly would object to characterisation of that. I'll let Mr. Jones continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him finish first, please. Let him finish, please. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, in that case, I think I could be finished in two and a half hours, I think that one and a half hours would be reasonable for the Prosecution, and then half an hour for re-examination and Judges' questions. That comes in my calculation to four and a half hours. We'll have 45 minutes today, three hours and 45 minutes tomorrow, that's four and a half hours. I would be content for Your Honour to switch off my microphone when I reach two and a half hours, provided you do the same to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you think we can do that Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour at this point, without having heard the witness's testimony, I'm not at this time in agreement with limiting my cross-examination to an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will fix a time ourselves. Okay. We will reconvene. Can I ask the indulgence of the staff to have a 20-minute break rather than 25? I see the French booth have signified yes, yes. And the recorder? Okay. Thank you. And the technicians, English booth?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Twenty minutes and we'll tell you exactly how much. So we'll have 45 minutes now and then 3 hours and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Jones and Ms. Richardson, we cannot allow ourselves to run the risk of having this witness start and not finish. So you will have two hours and 30 minutes, starting from when you start, and you will have one hour 25 minutes, and we are reserving 25 minutes for us or for other contingencies. Sir, good morning or good afternoon to you and welcome to this Tribunal. You are going to start giving evidence very soon. You've been brought forward here to give evidence by the Defence. Our Rules require that before you start giving evidence, you make a solemn declaration, equivalent to an oath in some jurisdictions, indicating your commitment with this Trial Chamber, with this Tribunal, that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration is being handed to you now by Madam Usher. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please make yourself comfortable. Today we will only be here for about 40 or 45 minutes. Then we will try to continue and finish tomorrow. Please try to restrict your answers to be as brief as possible, and try to answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question. Don't try to give more information than you were asked. First it will be Mr. Jones who will examine you in chief and then he will be followed by Ms. Richardson for the Prosecution on cross-examination. Your responsibility is to answer all questions truthfully and to the best of your ability irrespective of who is putting them to you. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Jones:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you may appreciate we are going to be quite short on time today and tomorrow and, so, as His Honour indicated, if you could give really a shorter answers as possible, really just if you can answer in a few words, that's best, and, if in doubt, err on the side of giving too short an answer than too long an answer. Now, please give your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can lead him on this, if you want, Mr. Jones, and get it over and done with.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: His name, what he's done, where and when was he born, and the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your name is Mirsad Mustafic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born on the 5th of March 1959 in Potocari in Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: On the 5th of March, 1959.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And incidentally is the name Mustafic common or uncommon in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: It's common.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are there other Mirsad Mustafics in your area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica municipality, I know about five people called Mirsad Mustafic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, your father's name is Nurdin [phoen] and your mother's name is Djeva [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Father, Nurdin; mother Djeva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it right that you attended primary school in Potocari and in Srebrenica, high school in Srebrenica, and you studied at the economics faculty in Sarajevo university between 1978 and 1983?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I won't go through your various occupations, but is it right that you worked in the construction industry among other things and that you also formed a housing cooperative in Srebrenica before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the war started, you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: When the war started, on the 16th, I went to Tuzla with my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you go to Tuzla? By road or by foot?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: In a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know if it was possible to reach Tuzla from Srebrenica by road after the 16th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: After the 16th of April, it was no longer possible. That was more or less the last day on which you could leave Srebrenica and go to Tuzla or some other place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the way to Tuzla, did you see anything of a Serb military presence?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: All along the road there were checkpoints, barricades, set up by the local Serb population, from Tisca towards Kladanj. There was a military unit stationed there and reservists, in the Lukic Polje area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say there was a military unit, do you know which unit, which Serb military unit?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: It was a military unit of the Uzice Corps and volunteers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just in terms of this area that you've mentioned --.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was considering using a map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I think it will be sufficient for our purposes if you tell us, is this anywhere near Sekovici, the Lukic Polje area you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: That's in the immediate vicinity of Sekovici on the regional road from Vlasenica to Kladanj. In Tisca you turn off towards Sekovici, and to get to Lukic Polje you go on in that direction towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it might assist if the witness could be quickly shown D895?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could we locate D895 and show it to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If that could please be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, witness, on this map, do you see first of all a road which has been highlighted and then an area marked in red?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't see the area marked in red on my monitor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you turn to your left and look at the map which is to your left on the ELMO. Now, if you locate first of all Zvornik -- I trust I can lead on this. If you go up, Witness, to Zvornik, you'll see Tuzla in the far left-hand corner, up the Drina, Zvornik. Now if you go left do you see the red marking there around the road to the left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see Sekovici? It's very small lettering but -- in any event. Now these barricades that you mentioned, was that in this area or in some other area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: The barricades were -- they started in Zuti Most in Bratunac municipality, and they were there all along the road, as far as Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the region of Lukevic Polje [phoen], which you said was in the Sekovici region, what did you see there, if you'll just remind us?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: There, I saw a military unit stationed there, which was already setting up tents. I saw a lot of military equipment and weaponry, and I saw quite a large number of soldiers in the uniforms worn by the reserve police force. They were unshaved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. And if the record could reflect that the witness was indicating with the marker or rather with the pointer the Sekovici area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I thank you. I confirm that, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was on the 16th of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's clarify one thing. We have been mentioning the 16ing of April. In the summary that you had circulated before, it mentions the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If that's so, this would be a correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know which one is the correct one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I think the witness can confirm this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the 16th of April or the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: The 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you arrive in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: I arrived in Tuzla late in the evening on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there many refugees in Tuzla when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes. In Tuzla, there was an enormous number of refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they only from Srebrenica, like yourself, or were they from other municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: They were from other neighbouring municipalities, Zvornik, Bratunac, Vlasenica and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as they were arriving, these refugees, was anyone taking care of or organising them and providing for accommodation, food, and their basic needs?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: At first, as large numbers of people kept arriving continuously in columns, the authorities of Tuzla municipality attempted to organise assistance initially they put them in a hall called Mejdan and in some empty schools.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were any associations set up to help these refugees?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: After a few days, when they saw that the number of people needing assistance was enormous, individual municipalities, which had fled to Tuzla, set up associations of refugees in Tuzla in order to attempt to assist the population there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you involved in one such association for refugees from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have any particular experience which equipped you to work, to do that sort of work?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: I did have a certain amount of experience. Before the war, I had been the president of the municipal trade union organisation which involved looking after workers and so I had some experience as did the other people who were at that time in the association of refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were associations also set up for refugees from Bratunac, from Vlasenica and from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes. The other municipalities also set up their own refugee associations in order to help their people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in April 1992, did this association have anything to do with mobilising people to fight in the Tuzla area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there actually war in the Tuzla area in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did war start in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: On that day, a column of the JNA arrived from Dubrave. It was passing through Tuzla and an incident occurred at Brcanska Malta, and on that day the war began in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 15th of May 1992, after that day, could you in Tuzla communicate with Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May 1992, was there telephone communication with Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: No. There was no telephone communication with Srebrenica as of the end of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, telephone communication between Tuzla and Srebrenica, which ceased in that period?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you personally try to reach anyone in Srebrenica in that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: I did try because my mother was there and other members of my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, if the witness could be shown P331, please. This is addressed to the republican TO staff in Sarajevo and to the regional TO staff in Tuzla, and there is a stamp from Sarajevo and various handwritten annotations at the top. First of all, because in English we have something written as "communications centre," can you confirm, witness, that the top of this document in handwriting at the very top, you see 27/10/00 but to the left there is simply the initials, the letters Č.V.?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: I don't know what this means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Simply to confirm that in English it says communications centre and we can test that as a translation. Now I just have one question on this document. Was it possible for a fax to be sent from Srebrenica to Tuzla on the 9th of July 1992? Sorry, this document is dated 9 July, 1992. Was it possible on that day for a fax to be sent from Srebrenica to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: No. It was not possible, in view of the fact that the telephone communications were cut off, so logically a fax could not have been sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you in fact ever see any faxes which had been received in Tuzla from Srebrenica after that period when communications were cut off, i.e. from May 1992 onwards, before demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could please now be shown Exhibit P234? And this is dated 3 July 1992, number 55, 92, and it's from the RBH municipal assembly Srebrenica TO staff to the Tuzla District Staff in Tuzla and I just want to read a short paragraphs, the first and third paragraph. "Since 10 April 1992, some 3.000 residents of Srebrenica municipality have fled to the Tuzla region escaping the aggression by Serbian Chetniks from Serbia and Montenegro and local SDS terrorists." I'm skipping paragraph 2. Paragraph 3, "On 5 June 1992, we in Tuzla have set up and registered the association of refugees, passed the necessary enactments, and selected organs in accordance with the statute. The association has been registered as a social and legal entity." Now firstly does that accurately reflect what happened in May and June 1992 or not, what's stated there?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was your association for refugees from Srebrenica registered as a legal entity?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you register with?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: The registration court in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have your own stamp?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we turn to page 2 of this document, do you know who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: The secretary of the association, Mr. Mehmed Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we have just seen this reference to the association of refugees. In the heading, there is a reference to Srebrenica TO staff. Can you explain to us what the relationship is between the Srebrenica TO staff mentioned here and the association of refugees which you formed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that in this period on the free territory of the Tuzla area, staffs were beginning to be set up, we too decided to establish a TO Staff which would join the cantonal or rather the district TO Staff of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say we. Who are you referring to when you say "we"?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to this association of refugees in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now were you a member of the TO staff which is referred to here, TO staff Srebrenica but in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a position at some stage?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: At a certain point I was a member of the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what the functions of the staff were?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: First of all, the functions of the staff were to have a unified register of all men liable for military service in the Tuzla district, all military-able men had to be listed, and these lists were to be handed over to the district secretariat for people's defence with a view to mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you also involved in the distribution of humanitarian aid to people in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes, apart from this, our basic task was to look after the people who found themselves in this area, meaning to provide humanitarian assistance, accommodation, food, clothing, footwear and everything else that was necessary for survival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the staff meet? When I say "staff" -- when I say "your staff," I'm referring to the Srebrenica municipality Territorial Defence staff in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: The seat was in Rudarska street in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the Vlasenica TO staff share the same building, at least for a period?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a period the municipal staff of Vlasenica was located there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we go back to this document, P234, if you look at the top right-hand corner of the document, you'll see 2207 in brackets, Sadic, and then look at this and let's consult. Do you see that, handwritten marks?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you actually see in English it says this is illegible but I don't believe it is, do you see a number before the 2207? Can you work out what number is written there?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Between the 2207 in brackets it's 01/795.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Do you know who Sadic is or who this might refer to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sadic was then the Chief of Staff of the Territorial Defence of the Tuzla district.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you keep that document with you --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for the assistance of the usher, if we could show the Witness P233. Now, this document again just for the record while it's being distributed is dated 2nd of July 1992, the last was dated 3rd of July 1992. The number on this document is 5692, it was 5529 on the last document and now we have to look just at the B/C/S for this next issue which is on page 3, it could be shown on the ELMO, otherwise we can look at our copy [inaudible] for us and the public gallery, but in any event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read for us what's written on that stamp, firstly, at the bottom left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: The date, 22nd July 1992, number 01/795.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it's the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina district territorial district staff, Territorial Defence, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The number, 01795, and the date corresponds to the document we just saw?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just dealing with this document, this stamp, does it appear that then on this date the 22nd of July 1992, is when these documents were apparently received by the District Staff, Territorial Defence, Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were received on the 22nd of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge, before that date, the 22nd of July 1992, did the Tuzla or was the Tuzla district TO staff aware of the municipal TO staff of Srebrenica that you had formed in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: No. It was on the date of receipt of this document that they learned about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we go back to P234, which I think you still have in front of you, the penultimate sentence of the last paragraph on the first page in English it says, "We are ready to place ourselves at the disposal of the Tuzla TO district staff on whose territory there are some 40 fighters from Srebrenica." Do you see that in B/C/S? It's on the first page, [B/C/S spoken]. Do you see that? If you go to the bottom and then count up about seven lines, seven lines from the bottom [B/C/S spoken]? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct then that certainly as of the 22nd of July 1992, when this was received, that the -- your staff was not a part of the Tuzla TO District Defence Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Our staff was not a part of the District Defence Staff until the 27th of July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so then, at that point, was it a question of the Tuzla TO district defence staff establishing a subordinate organ, a Srebrenica Municipal TO Staff or of an organ calling itself the Srebrenica Municipal Defence Staff forming itself and volunteering to be part of the Tuzla staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we were within the territory of the Tuzla district, the only way of assisting in the defence against the aggression was to get ourselves organised in this Municipal Staff in Tuzla where we basically placed ourselves at the disposal of the District Staff of the TO Tuzla, and we did it on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So in other words the TO Tuzla didn't form you; you formed yourself and then volunteered to be part of it?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we go again back to P233 which I think you still have before you, there is a reference to the formation of a Rudarska Srebrenica company. Are you familiar with that company?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what if anything is the relationship between that organ, that company, and the -- and your staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: We established the unit to be able to join the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is this unit, the people who are mentioned, are they people in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes. All these people were in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did this staff and this company have anything to do with any fighters physically present in Srebrenica municipality, Srebrenica municipality, at that time, in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Nothing to do at all. Whatever is mentioned here was exclusively linked with Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again turning to the signature, do you recognise who signed this?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Mehmed Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same one you told us about before?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the stamp we see here, do you recognise that or not, as your stamp for your staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is our stamp, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this document actually prepared in Tuzla or in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: Only in Tuzla and it applies to all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the people mentioned in this document assigned from Srebrenica or were they assigned by you in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD MUSTAFIC
utterances.text: We appointed these people at a meeting that we held. It was us.
